item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 190508
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sun Oct 18 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Trudy, located about 150 miles offshore of the coast of Jalisco,
Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
Disorganized showers and thunderstorms have persisted with an area
of disturbed weather located several hundred miles south of
Guatemala. Environmental conditions appear conducive for
development, and a tropical depression is expected to form around
the middle of this week as the system moves westward to
west-northwestward at around 10 mph, well to the south of the coast
of southern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Public Advisory Number 24
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Mon Oct 19 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 190831
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Trudy Advisory Number  24
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
200 AM MST Mon Oct 19 2026
 
...TRUDY RAPIDLY WEAKENING...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.7N 108.0W
ABOUT 155 MI...250 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Trudy was
located near latitude 19.7 North, longitude 108.0 West. Trudy is
moving toward the west near 6 mph (9 km/h) and this motion is
expected to continue through tonight, followed by a gradual turn 
toward the northwest on Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 60 mph (95 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Rapid weakening is expected to continue today, 
and Trudy is forecast to degenerate to a post-tropical cyclone by 
tonight.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy will continue affecting portions of
the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico through today.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 23
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Sun Oct 18 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 190244
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number  23
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
800 PM MST Sun Oct 18 2026
 
Examining the last-light visible satellite imagery of Trudy, it is 
becoming clear that the hurricane is starting to rapidly weaken. The 
coldest cloud tops within the cyclone on infrared imagery are now 
around -55 degrees C, and the convection continues to decline at a 
steady rate. This degradation in Trudy's structure is likely due to 
a combination of the southwesterly shear and some dry air intrusion 
into the core of the cyclone. Using a combination of the objective 
and subjective intensity estimates, the intensity has been lowered 
to 70 kt for this advisory.
 
A WSF-M microwave pass at 0040 UTC was very useful in locating the 
center of Trudy, which was further south and west of the Dvorak 
position, though the initial motion is still estimated towards the 
northwest or 315/6 kt. A turn toward the west-northwest or west 
along with a decrease in forward speed is expected to occur as Trudy 
continues to weaken. As the cyclone weakens, low- to mid-level flow 
will become the main steering for Trudy. Trudy will continue to move 
away from west-central Mexico, and then move south of Baja 
California Sur over the next day or so. The current NHC track 
forecast is farther south of the previous one, partially due to the 
adjustment in the initial position, but remains in good agreement 
with the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids.
 
The hurricane already appears to be rapidly weakening due to the 
influence of southwesterly shear along with a drier and more stable 
airmass. The current NHC intensity forecast is in the middle of the 
guidance envelope showing Trudy continuing to rapidly weaken over 
the next day or so, followed by more gradual weakening. The current 
forecast has Trudy becoming post-tropical in 48 h and then 
dissipating in 72 h. However, it is possible that both of these 
events could occur sooner than currently predicted.
 
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Heavy rainfall from Trudy is subsiding along the southwest 
Mexican coast in Jalisco, and the associated flood risk is expected 
to diminish as well
 
2. Large swells will continue to affect the coast of southwestern
Mexico and west-central Mexico during the next two to three days,
causing life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  19/0300Z 19.7N 107.6W   70 KT  80 MPH
 12H  19/1200Z 19.8N 107.9W   60 KT  70 MPH
 24H  20/0000Z 19.8N 108.5W   45 KT  50 MPH
 36H  20/1200Z 19.9N 109.3W   40 KT  45 MPH
 48H  21/0000Z 20.4N 109.8W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 60H  21/1200Z 21.1N 110.1W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 72H  22/0000Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Papin
